//: The target profile: inference on the devbox's RTX 5070 instead of this laptop's CPU. Run with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Target, which is what loads this file over appsettings.json. Nothing else changes, because every mind call carries its whole context and the server holds no colony state.

Simulation.//: A seed for the Contemplation readout until enough calls have been served to measure it live.

Mind.//Endpoint: Ollama on the devbox listens on localhost only, so it is reached through a tunnel: ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:11436:127.0.0.1:11434 devbox. The tunnel lives as long as that ssh process does — when it dies, every call falls back and the colony keeps running without a mind, which is the whole point of the fallbacks but is not what you wanted.
Mind.//TokensPerMinute: 14000 against the laptop's 3600. The ceiling is a per-machine measured figure; left at 3600 the governor would throttle a GPU that can serve several times that.
Mind.//DeepModel: Measured 24 October 2026 and deliberately NOT gemma4:12b, which this file used to name. gemma4 is thinking-capable — the first such model the project has actually run — and reproduces the M0 trap exactly: with think on it spends 440 characters reasoning, hits its cap and returns unparseable JSON. LaneConfig.Think defaults to false so that is handled. What is not handled is the cap: on the deliberation shape gemma4 writes a mean of 118 tokens against a cap of 128 and parsed 5 of 6, while llama3.2:3b writes a mean of 52 and parsed 6 of 6. At 256 gemma4 parsed 6 of 6 with a max of 155. So moving the deep lane to a 12B model is a real upgrade and it needs CallBudgets raised with it — its own milestone, not a side effect of changing where inference happens.
